A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RePo: Language Models with Context Re-Positioning. All 17 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original OLMo-2 evaluations, attention and position analyses, layer-placement ablations, and GPT-2 text-reversal experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports qualitative outcomes from alternative RePo layer placements.

M1.justification: The position-representation and assignment modules, attention computation in Equations 4–7, training approach and autoregressive inference procedure are retained. The revised starting-layer notation retains the explicit 5th/10th-layer defaults; alternative placements are reported as preliminary tests.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluated coverage remain unchanged: RULER, HybridQA, LongBench, general benchmarks and synthetic text reversal. The new schematic illustrates the existing reversal task, and the added layer-placement tests establish no additional task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain RoPE, NoPE, R2N1 and N2R1 for OLMo-2 1B, RoPE for 7B, and RoPE/NoPE for synthetic reversal. Newly cited methods are not added to the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, footnote 4 newly reports experimental configurations using RePo in very few layers or only the first third, with standard RoPE in the remaining layers. Existing benchmark protocols, training budgets, metrics and appendix settings are retained; no rerunning of those evaluations is established.

E4.justification: The new Section 4.1 footnote adds qualitative layer-placement tests: using very few RePo layers gives performance close to RoPE, while using only the first third makes training unstable. These supplement the retained starting-layer sensitivity analysis in Appendix B.5; the other analyses and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Point estimates and descriptive position distributions retain the same reporting practices; the added relative-error calculation does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 swaps MQ/MV headings without swapping the 1B entries: RePo’s reported MQ/MV scores consequently change from 89.3/89.8 to 89.8/89.3. The 7B task-matched scores and Table 1 averages remain unchanged. The new layer-placement footnote adds qualitative outcomes; other tables and existing plot results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, Appendix A’s NoPE reformulation and the position-pattern definitions are unchanged. The added discussion of low-frequency RoPE extrapolation is a qualitative explanation, without a new derivation, formal assumption or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same lightweight, differentiable repositioning contribution, improvements on noisy, structured and long-context tasks, and competitive general-task performance. The abstract’s attention-burden wording reframes the motivation without changing the contribution or empirical scope.

C2.justification: v3 presents CLT more as an additional interpretation, expands the hypothesis connecting dense positions to low-frequency RoPE extrapolation, and interprets the unchanged 0.6-point 7B improvement as a 22% reduction in remaining errors. The new placement outcomes also document configurations with little benefit or unstable training.

D1.justification: v3 specifies that Section 5 analyses use the 1B model, discloses purposeful selection of Figure 9 examples, and writes the starting-layer rule as ceil(L/3). The code link remains, but the explicit promise to release model weights is removed; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hyönä and Lorch (2004), Schneider et al. (2018), and Li et al. (2026) on HoPE for vision-language models, while removing Miller (1956), Dubey et al. (2024), and Meta (2025). These are limited changes to motivational support and citations; positioning relative to CoPE and other positional methods remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and opening rationale are locally rewritten, explanations and grammar receive limited edits, a conflict-of-interest disclosure is added, and acknowledgments are revised. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds an architecture schematic as Figure 1. Table 3 uses abbreviated dataset headings with a caption key and larger type; other tables receive formatting and highlighting changes, and some displays move. Existing plots are retained and renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new architecture schematic, more legible tables, and disclosures about unsuccessful layer placements and case-study selection provide limited improvements in clarity and transparency. The central benchmark evidence remains largely unchanged. Table 1’s unexplained MQ/MV reassignment and removal of the model-weight release promise temper these gains.
